checks.note: RefundEnqueueListener confirms the narrow claim: its four @TransactionalEventListener methods cover parent/coach/admin-cancel and coach-no-show only, with no BookingCancelledDueToPauseEvent handler. But the finding's consequence depends on PackSessionService.pausePackTransactional, PaymentLifecycleService settle behavior, CancellationRefundService's event handlers, and a repo-wide grep for other pause-event consumers — none of which were provided, so the required verification cannot be run.

The file confirms the mechanism: all four AFTER_COMMIT/REQUIRES_NEW handlers call packSessionService.restoreSession bare (unlike issueStrikeSafely's catch of PessimisticLockingFailureException), and in onBookingCancelledByCoach a restore failure skips saveCancellationHistory and the strike. But the finding's required verification — that no scheduler/outbox (RefundOutboxSupport) reconciles CANCELLED pack bookings, and that restoreSession really uses an exhaustible NOWAIT PESSIMISTIC_WRITE retry — depends on PackSessionService and RefundOutboxSupport code not shown here.

The trigger is real in this file: cancelBookingAsCoach and recordNoShowCoach compute packExpired from pack.getExpiresAt().isBefore(Instant.now()) before the transition commits, and createBookingRequest does reject expired packs (payment.packExpired), satisfying half the verification caveat. But the consequence depends on CancellationRefundService.restoreSession (AFTER_COMMIT, no expiry extension), RefundEnqueueListener keying refunds solely off the event's packExpired flag, and whether any job converts expired-pack remaining sessions to credit — none of which is in this file.
